positions.lease_says: Assignment and subletting need Owner's consent and Owner has a recapture right and a 50 percent profit share, but Tenant may transfer without consent to affiliates, subsidiaries and successors, and may rescind its request to defeat a recapture.
positions.proposed_response: Apply a net worth test to all consent-free affiliate and subsidiary transfers (not only successors), delete Tenant's right to rescind after Owner elects recapture, confirm the 50 percent share of transfer profit without the sale-of-business carve-out, and correct the paragraph lettering and cross-references in Article 52.
quotes: Tenant may, without Owner’s consent and on not less than ten (10) days prior written notice to Owner

an entity which shall be an “affiliate”, “subsidiary” or “successor” (each as hereinafter defined) of Tenant and the provisions of Paragraphs (a), (b) and (c) of this Article shall be inapplicable to such transaction
Tenant shall have the right to rescind the Tenant request to assign the Lease or sublease the Premises which gave rise to such exercise by Owner
positions.why: The consent-free affiliate and subsidiary transfer carries no net worth test (only successors must meet one), Tenant can withdraw its request to defeat recapture, and the 50 percent share excludes consideration paid for the business in a sale of Tenant's business. Paragraph lettering in Article 52 is inconsistent (two "(a)" paragraphs; cross-references to (f), (h) and (j) do not match), which should be fixed.

positions.lease_says: The premises may be used only for general and executive offices.
quotes: General and executive offices and for no other purpose.
Tenant shall use and occupy the demised premises only for the Permitted Use as set forth in the Basic Lease Provisions Section of this lease and for no other purpose.
positions.why: Use is limited to office use with no other purpose allowed, which matches the standard position.

positions.lease_says: All changes need Owner's prior written consent, but a rider note makes that consent not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed for interior non-structural work that does not affect Building systems.
positions.proposed_response: Delete Note 1 or limit the reasonableness standard to purely decorative work, and confirm Owner's consent to all other alterations is in its sole discretion, with Tenant paying Owner's review and supervision costs under Articles 50 and 59.
quotes: Tenant shall, make no changes in or to the demised premises of any nature without Owner’s prior written consent.

which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed in the case of interior, non-structural work to be performed wholly within the demised premises, which work does not affect the proper functioning of any Building system or equipment or that of any other tenant of the Building
positions.why: Owner's discretion over non-structural interior work is limited to a reasonableness standard, so Owner keeps full discretion only over structural or building-system work. The footnote markers were lost in the filing, so where Note 1 is inserted in Article 3 is inferred rather than shown.

positions.lease_says: Tenant must remove specialty alterations and repair the damage at its cost unless Owner agreed in writing, at Tenant's request when consent was sought, that removal is not required.
quotes: unless Owner shall agree to the contrary in writing following Tenant’s specific request as to whether Tenant shall be required to remove the proposed alteration

Tenant shall be required to remove, no later than thirty (30) days prior to the Expiration Date or earlier termination of the Term, any vaults and raised floors, kitchens, kitchen appliances and pantries, staircases, antennas or any other “specialty” installations or alterations
positions.why: Removal applies by default and is waived only if Owner affirmatively agrees, so Owner's failure to designate items does not release Tenant.

positions.lease_says: Tenant pays its proportionate share of operating expense increases over a base year, now calendar year 2019, with no cap.
quotes: pay to Owner as additional rent at the times hereinafter specified an amount (the “Operating Payment”) equal to Tenant’s Proportionate Share of the Operating Expenses for the then current Lease Year or calendar year (as the case may be) that are in excess of the Operating Expenses for the Operating Base Year
the Operating Base Year (as defined in the Basic Lease Provisions) shall be the calendar year 2019
positions.why: No cap applies, and the 95 percent gross-up in 38(c) applies to comparison periods rather than favoring Tenant on the base year. The base year was reset in the amendments, which the standard does not address.

positions.lease_says: No actual real estate taxes are payable, so Tenant instead pays its proportionate share of the increase in assessed value times tax rate over a base tax year, now fiscal 2019/20, and Owner may recalculate if the Tax Base is reduced.
quotes: In lieu of a real estate tax escalation, Tenant hereby covenants and agrees to pay to Owner as additional rent on the first day of each and every month during the Term an amount equal to the quotient obtained by dividing the amount of the Taxes applicable to the then current Lease Year by the number of months in such Lease Year.
If the Tax Base is at any time reduced for any reason whatsoever, Owner shall have the right to adjust the amount of each of Tenant’s payments previously made on account of Taxes
The definition of “Tax Base Year” set forth in the Basic Lease Provisions shall be amended to read as follows: “Fiscal year July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020.
positions.why: The payment tracks the standard escalation over a base year, and Owner may adjust if the base drops. The base year was reset in the 2018 and 2019 amendments, which shifts earlier increases to Owner, but this was done as part of renewal terms rather than as a reduction mechanism.

positions.lease_says: Tenant has posted a cash deposit, now $220,619.00, that Owner may apply on any default, and there is no burn-down.
quotes: in the event Tenant defaults in respect of any of the terms, provisions and conditions of this lease, including, but not to, the payment of rent and additional rent Owner may use, ap4 or retain the whole or any part of the security so deposited
thereby increasing the cash security held by Landlord under the Lease to $220,619.00
positions.why: Cash security is held for the full term with a draw right on default and no reduction, which meets or exceeds the standard. The letter of credit draw in 54(a) requires a default beyond notice and cure, but it applies only if Tenant replaces the cash.

positions.lease_says: Tenant carries general liability insurance of at least $3,000,000 per occurrence naming Owner and its managing agent as additional insureds, and both parties waive recovery to the extent of their insurance.
positions.proposed_response: Increase Tenant's commercial general liability coverage to at least $5,000,000 per occurrence (primary plus umbrella), keeping Owner, its managing agent and superior parties as additional insureds.
quotes: naming Owner (as that term was broadly defined for purposes of this Article only) and Owner’s current managing agent, TF Cornerstone Inc., and any future managing agent, as additional insureds, in limits (subject to increase at Owner’s reasonable request) of not less than $3,000,000 combined single limit for bodily and personal injury or death and for property damage per occurrence
Owner hereby waives any and all right of recovery which it might otherwise have against Tenant, its servants, agents and employees, for loss or damage occurring to the Building
positions.why: The $3,000,000 limit is below the $5,000,000 standard. Additional insured status and a mutual waiver of subrogation are in place.

positions.lease_says: Tenant indemnifies Owner for claims arising from its use and control of the premises and from the acts of its people, and Owner gives no general indemnity.
quotes: covenants and agrees to indemnify and hold Owner harmless from and against all claims, actions, judgments, damages, liabilities or expenses including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys’ fees, in connection with damage to property or injury or death to persons, arising from or out of the use, alteration, occupation, management, possession or control of the demised premises
positions.why: Tenant's indemnity is broad and not limited to gross negligence. Owner's only indemnity is the mutual brokerage indemnity in the amendments.

positions.lease_says: Tenant's recovery is limited to Owner's interest in the Building, and Owner is not liable for consequential damages on injury or property loss claims.
quotes: Tenant shall look only to Owner’s estate and interest in the Building for the satisfaction of Tenant’s remedies or for the collection of a judgment (or other judicial process) requiring the payment of money by Owner
in no event shall any of the Indemnitees ever be liable with respect to any claim for consequential damages in connection therewith
positions.why: Recovery is limited to Owner's interest in the Building, as the standard requires. The consequential damages exclusion is tied to the injury and property claims in 43(c) rather than stated for all claims, which the partner may want to broaden.

positions.lease_says: After a default notice and a cure period (apparently amended by rider notes to 10 days for money defaults and a longer period, likely 20 days, for other defaults, extended while Tenant diligently cures), Owner must serve a separate 5-day cancellation notice.
positions.proposed_response: Provide that a single default notice with a 10-day cure for monetary defaults and a 30-day diligence-qualified cure for other defaults is sufficient, and confirm how Notes 11 to 14 amend Article 17.
quotes: upon Owner serving a written fifteen (15) days’ notice upon Tenant specifying the nature of said default
then Owner may serve a written five (5) days’ notice of cancellation of this lease upon Tenant
in the case of default not involving the payment of a money or ten (10) days in the case of any default involving the payment of money
positions.why: The cure periods are within the standard, but terminating requires a second notice. The footnote markers were lost in the filing, so how Notes 11 to 14 modify Article 17 is inferred.

positions.lease_says: Owner restores after a casualty, rent abates according to the usable part of the premises, only Owner may terminate, and Tenant waives its statutory termination right.
quotes: the damages thereto shall be repaired by, and at the expense of, Owner, and the rent and other items of additional rent, until such repair shall be substantially complete, shall be apportioned from the day following the casualty
Owner may elect to terminate this lease by written notice to Tenant
Tenant hereby waives the provisions of Section 227 of the Real Property Law
positions.why: Tenant has no termination right at all and abatement is tied to the unusable space, which gives Owner more than the standard.

positions.lease_says: A holdover Tenant pays 250 percent of the last year's rent and is liable for all of Owner's losses, including claims by succeeding tenants.
quotes: all losses and damages which Owner may incur or sustain by reason thereof
per diem use and occupancy in respect of the demised premises equal to two and one-half (2 1/2) times the Base Rent and additional rent payable hereunder for the last year of the Term
positions.why: Holdover rent exceeds 150 percent from day one, and Tenant is liable for damages with no grace period.

positions.lease_says: The lease and its amendments grant no renewal, expansion, first offer or termination options, and any option is void during a default.
quotes: Tenant shall not be entitled to exercise any right of termination or other option granted to it by this lease (if any) at any time when Tenant is in default
positions.why: Term extensions and added space were agreed by negotiated amendments rather than options, so Tenant holds no unilateral rights.

positions.lease_says: New York law governs, and both parties waive a jury trial except for personal injury or property damage claims.
quotes: This lease shall be governed in all respects by the internal laws of the State of New York.

the respective parties hereto shall, and they hereby do, waive trial by jury in any action proceeding or counterclaim brought by either of the parties hereto against the other (except for personal injury or property damage)
positions.why: New York law and a mutual jury waiver are in place. The personal injury and property damage carve-out is the standard printed-form exception.

positions.lease_says: Transfers need Landlord's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld and deemed granted after 30 days of silence; Landlord may recapture on an assignment or a sublet for substantially the balance of the Term and takes 50% of net profit; affiliate transfers need no consent or net worth test, and mergers need none if a net worth test is met.
positions.proposed_response: Add a net worth test to the related-corporation transfer in Subsection 12.L. Extend the recapture right in Subsection 12.C to any sublease of all or substantially all of the Premises regardless of term. Delete the deemed-consent sentence in Subsection 12.G, or condition it on a second notice carrying a bold-face warning and a further response period.
quotes: Tenant may, without Landlord's consent, but upon written notice to Landlord, permit any corporations or other business entities (but not including Governmental Entities) which control, are controlled by, or are under common control with Tenant (herein referred to as "related corporation") to receive an assignment of this Lease or to sublet all or part of the Premises

terminate this Lease and recapture the entire Premises in the event of an assignment of the Lease, or the applicable portion thereof, in the event of a sublet for substantially the balance of the Term.
in the event Landlord fails to respond within such thirty (30) day period, Landlord’s consent to the proposed assignment or sublease shall be deemed granted.
positions.why: The recapture right and 50% profit share match the standard, but the affiliate transfer right has no net worth test, recapture does not reach shorter or partial-term sublets, and the deemed-consent provision goes beyond the standard.

positions.lease_says: Use is limited to general, executive and administrative offices and no other purpose.
quotes: "Permitted Uses" shall mean general, executive and administrative office use only.
Tenant agrees to use and occupy the Premises for the Permitted Uses, and for no other purpose.
positions.why: This matches the standard position.

positions.lease_says: Alterations need Landlord's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, except cosmetic work under $50,000 per project or six-month series; plans are deemed approved after 15 days of silence, and Landlord's review costs are capped at $3,500.
positions.proposed_response: Limit consent-free work to purely decorative painting and carpeting, or cap Minor Alterations at a small per-project amount and expressly exclude anything touching Building systems or structure. Remove the $3,500 cap on Landlord's reasonable review costs. Delete the 15-day deemed approval, or require a second notice with a further response period.
quotes: Notwithstanding the foregoing, Tenant shall not be required to obtain Landlord’s consent for repainting, recarpeting, or other alterations, tenant improvements, alterations or physical additions to the Premises which are cosmetic in nature totaling less than $50,000 in any single instance or series of related alterations performed within a six-month period (“Minor Alterations”)
in connection with Landlord's review of Tenant's plans and specifications, capped at $3,500.00

In the event Landlord fails to respond to Tenant's request for consent to Alterations within fifteen (15) days of Tenant's submission to Landlord of Tenant's plans, said plans ... shall deemed to be approved by Landlord
positions.why: The consent-free category reaches $50,000, well above a low threshold. Review-cost recovery is capped, and approval can be deemed by silence.

positions.lease_says: Tenant must remove Specialty Alterations, including vaults and internal staircases, at its cost and repair any damage caused by removal, without any designation requirement.
quotes: Tenant shall be obligated to remove Specialty Alterations from the Premises, at Tenant's expense, prior to the Expiration Date.

“Specialty Alterations” shall include Alterations consisting of kitchens, pantries, executive bathrooms, computer installations, safe deposit boxes, vaults, libraries or file rooms requiring reinforcement of floors, internal staircases, conveyors, dumbwaiters and other Alterations of a similar character
positions.why: Removal is automatic rather than tied to designation at the time of consent, which matches the standard. Supplemental HVAC is not named but falls within the catch-all for alterations of a similar character.

positions.lease_says: The escalation article covers only real estate taxes, so Tenant pays no operating expense escalation beyond the fixed base rent steps in Exhibit D, electricity and specific charges.
positions.proposed_response: Add an operating expense escalation under which Tenant pays its 9% Proportionate Share of increases over a base year, with no cap on controllable expenses, or confirm that the fixed rent steps were agreed in lieu of it.
quotes: shall mean the amounts payable by Tenant on account of Tenant’s Proportionate Share of Taxes as described in Article 28 herein, the Electric Charges as described in Article 30 herein

If the Taxes payable for any Comparison Year (any part or all of which falls within the Term) shall represent an increase above the Base Taxes, then the Rent for such Comparison Year and continuing thereafter until a new Landlord's Statement is rendered to Tenant, shall be increased by Tenant's Proportionate Share of such increase.
positions.why: Tenant pays no share of increases in operating expenses, which is a listed departure. The fixed annual rent increases (about 3.5%) may have been the commercial trade-off for this.

positions.lease_says: Tenant pays 9% of increases in Taxes over the 2023/2024 Base Tax Year, the base is not reduced by later assessment reductions, and the escalation is waived if no statement is sent within three years.
quotes: "Base Tax Year" shall mean the Taxes payable for the 2023/2024 Tax Year
the Base Taxes shall not be reduced to reflect such reduction.

Tenant shall be relieved of any obligation to pay Tenant’s Proportionate Share of Taxes for a Comparison Year in question if a Landlord’s Statement is not delivered by Landlord to Tenant within three (3) years of the due date for Taxes.
positions.why: This matches the standard, and the no-reduction-of-base clause favors Landlord. The three-year billing deadline is a minor tenant protection to note.

positions.lease_says: Tenant posts $80,000 in cash or as an unconditional letter of credit, Landlord may draw on an Event of Default, and there is no burn-down.
quotes: "Security Deposit" shall mean $80,000.00.
The Letter of Credit shall be issued by a bank approved by Landlord and shall be clean, unconditional, irrevocable, freely transferable

In the Event of a Default, in addition to any or all of its other remedies contained in this Lease, Landlord shall have the right (but not the obligation) to draw down on the Cash Deposit or present the Letter of Credit for payment and to draw thereon, in whole or in part.
positions.why: Drawing is tied to an Event of Default, meaning after notice and cure, which the standard allows, and there is no reduction schedule.

positions.lease_says: Tenant carries commercial general liability insurance of $3,000,000 per occurrence naming Landlord and its managing agent as additional insureds, and the waiver of subrogation is mutual.
positions.proposed_response: Increase the commercial general liability limit to not less than $5,000,000 per occurrence, which may be met through primary and umbrella coverage.
quotes: The minimum limits of liability shall be a combined single limit with respect to each occurrence in an amount of not less than $3,000,000.00 per occurrence.

Landlord, Landlord's managing agent, the present and any future mortgagee of the Real Property or the Building and/or such other designees specified by Landlord, from time to time, as additional insureds
Landlord and Tenant each waives any claim it might have against the other
positions.why: The additional insureds and mutual waiver match the standard, but the $3,000,000 limit is below the $5,000,000 standard.

positions.lease_says: Tenant gives a broad indemnity for its acts, the Premises and its breaches, and Landlord indemnifies Tenant for Losses from any act, omission or negligence of Landlord or its agents, contractors or employees and from Landlord's breach.
positions.proposed_response: Limit Landlord's indemnity in Subsection 37.B to Losses caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of Landlord or its agents, contractors or employees, and clarify the 'and arising from any breach' wording.
quotes: Subject to Subsection C of Article 9 above, Landlord shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Tenant and its representatives and agents from and against each and every Loss arising out of any act, omission or negligence of Landlord, or any of its agents, contractors or employees
Tenant shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Landlord and its representatives and agents from and against all liabilities
positions.why: Tenant's indemnity matches the standard. Landlord's indemnity covers any act or omission, not only negligence or willful misconduct, although the conjunctive 'and arising from any breach' wording makes its scope unclear.

positions.lease_says: Landlord's liability is limited to direct damages recoverable only from its interest in the Building and the Real Property, and neither party is liable for consequential damages except under the holdover article.
quotes: shall only be recoverable from Landlord's interest in the Building and the Real Property and Tenant shall not look to or attach any other property or assets of Landlord
In no event shall Landlord or Tenant ... ever be liable for incidental or consequential damages, except as provided in Article 21 herein.
positions.why: This matches the standard. The mutual consequential-damages waiver carves out holdover, which preserves Landlord's claims against Tenant.

positions.lease_says: Tenant has 10 days after one notice to cure a rent default and 30 days after notice to cure other defaults, extended only while it diligently prosecutes a cure.
quotes: such default shall continue for a period of ten (10) days following written notice from Landlord to Tenant

Tenant shall fail to remedy such default within thirty (30) days after notice by Landlord to Tenant of such default, or if such default is of such a nature that it cannot be completely remedied within said period of thirty (30) days and Tenant shall not commence within said period of thirty (30) days, or shall not thereafter diligently prosecute
positions.why: This matches the standard. The later ten-day termination notice is the usual conditional-limitation mechanism, not a second cure notice.

positions.lease_says: Tenant may terminate if repairs are estimated to take more than 180 days, are not finished within 180 days, or the casualty occurs in the final Lease Year, and rent abates only for the untenantable portion.
positions.proposed_response: Extend Tenant's termination trigger to restoration not completed within at least 12 months. Limit the final-Lease-Year right to material damage that cannot be repaired within a stated period.
quotes: Landlord estimates that the damage caused thereby cannot be repaired within one hundred eighty (180) days after the commencement of repairs (the "Repair Period"), or if in fact the damage is not actually fully repaired by Landlord within one hundred eighty (180) days of the date of occurrence of the Casualty, or if the Casualty occurs during the final Lease Year
rent for the portion of the Premises rendered untenantable by the damage shall be abated on a reasonable basis
positions.why: Rent abatement matches the standard, but the 180-day termination trigger is well short of 12 months, and the final-year trigger adds another early exit.

positions.lease_says: Holdover rent is 150% of Rent for the first 30 days and 200% thereafter, and Tenant indemnifies Landlord, including for lost profits and successor-tenant claims, if it holds over more than 30 days.
quotes: a sum equal to (i) one and one-half (1.5) times the aggregate of that portion of the Rent for the first 30 days of such holdover, and 100% of the Additional Rent which was payable under this Lease during the last month of the Term, and (ii) two (2) times the aggregate of that portion of the Rent for any time thereafter
for more than thirty (30) days following the Expiration Date, Tenant shall protect, defend, indemnify and hold Landlord harmless from all loss
positions.why: The rent level, the step-up and the damages exposure after a short grace period match the standard. Additional Rent is charged at 100%, not at the enhanced rate.

positions.lease_says: Tenant has a one-time option to terminate effective at the end of the month after the second anniversary of the Commencement Date, on six months' notice and payment of a three-month fee; the option is personal and conditioned on no Event of Default.
positions.proposed_response: Confirm the client approved the Termination Option. Require that no Event of Default exist on the Termination Date as well as on exercise. Consider increasing the Termination Fee to cover unamortized brokerage commissions and Landlord's Work costs.
quotes: Tenant shall have a one-time option to terminate this Lease (the “Termination Option”).
a termination fee equal to three (3) months of the then escalated Rent and Additional Rent due from Tenant as of the Termination Date (the “Termination Fee”)
The Termination Option is reserved to Tenant and will not inure to the benefit of any sublessees, transferees, successors and/or assigns of Tenant.
positions.why: Any early termination right is a departure unless Landlord approved it, though the right is already personal and conditioned on no Event of Default.

positions.lease_says: New York law governs, venue is New York County, and both parties waive a jury trial.
quotes: shall be construed in accordance with the laws of New York.
It is mutually agreed by and between Landlord and Tenant that the respective parties hereto shall and they hereby do waive trial by jury
positions.why: This matches the standard position.

positions.lease_says: Use is executive and general office plus open-ended 'customary ancillary uses', including a non-exhaustive list: cafeterias without cooking, serving alcohol to Permitted Users, data centers, printing, an exercise facility, and recording and video studios.

Such ancillary uses may include, without limitation, the following uses

recording and video studios (provided that Tenant shall cause such recording and video studios to be operated and constructed so that no noise or vibration will emanate from the Premises to other portions of the Building)

However, the ancillary-use grant is open-ended ('without limitation', 'as shall be reasonably required by Tenant') and covers non-office uses such as studios, a gym, data centers and alcohol service, instead of a closed list of approved exceptions.

positions.lease_says: Consent is required for Alterations but cannot be unreasonably withheld for non-structural, non-systems work. Decorative and workstation/data work up to $250,000 ($400,000 after expansion), CPI-adjusted, needs no consent, and consent is deemed given after a second unanswered notice.
positions.proposed_response: Require Landlord's consent for all non-decorative Alterations. If a consent-free category is kept, cap it at a small per-project amount and exclude anything touching structure or Building Systems. Delete the deemed-consent mechanism in Section 8.02(i).
quotes: Landlord will not unreasonably withhold or delay approval of written requests of Tenant to make Alterations that (1) do not affect the Building’s exterior (including the appearance), (2) do not adversely affect any Building Systems, (3) are non-structural

Landlord’s consent shall not be required with respect to Non-Material Alterations which (w) do not require a building permit or a change in the certificate of occupancy for the Building, (x) do not cost in excess of (I) $250,000.00 (Subject to CPI Increases) or (II) from and after the Expansion Space Inclusion Date, $400,000.00 (Subject to CPI Increases)
then Landlord shall be deemed to have consented to the Alteration in question and the Tenant’s Plans with respect thereto.

positions.lease_says: Tenant must remove listed Specialty Alterations (kitchens, raised floors, vaults, extra staircases, slab penetrations and similar items) at its cost and repair the damage. One internal staircase is excluded, and non-listed items escape removal if Landlord fails to designate them in response to Tenant's time-sensitive notice.
positions.proposed_response: Include all internal staircases and supplemental HVAC as enumerated Specialty Alterations. Delete the deemed waiver in Section 8.01(iv) so that Tenant removes specialty alterations at its cost whether or not Landlord designated them at the time of consent.
quotes: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Lease to the contrary, Tenant shall not be obligated to remove any Alterations, except, subject to the provisions of this Section 8.01(iii) and Section 12.01, Specialty Alterations.
internal staircases (provided, that one internal staircase in the Premises shall not constitute a Specialty Alteration, but any additional internal staircase shall constitute a Specialty Alteration)
then, in either case, Tenant shall not be required to remove or pay for the removal of such Alterations which are not so designated as Specialty Alterations.
positions.why: The removal obligation exists for the enumerated items, but the first internal staircase is carved out. Supplemental HVAC is not enumerated and falls under the catch-all, which Landlord waives if it fails to designate the item when Tenant sends its notice.

positions.lease_says: Tenant pays its Percentage of all Expenses each Expense Year, with no base year and no cap, and Expenses are grossed up for unfurnished services.

the Expenses for such Expense Year shall be increased by an amount equal to the additional expenses which would reasonably have been incurred during such Expense Year by Landlord if Landlord had at its own expense furnished such item of work or service to the entire Project.
positions.why: A full pass-through with no base year and no cap gives Landlord more than the standard. However, the definition of 'Percentage' in 48.02(i) has a redacted sentence that may modify the share.

positions.lease_says: Tenant pays Tenant's Share of all Real Estate Taxes each Tax Year from the Rent Commencement Date, with no base year, and the taxes are computed without regard to incentive abatements.

Real Estate Taxes shall be calculated without taking into account any exemption, abatement or reduction which the Project or any portion thereof may now or hereafter receive pursuant to any governmental incentive program
positions.why: A full tax pass-through with no base year, ignoring abatements, gives Landlord more than the standard. However, a redacted sentence in the Tenant's Share definition (32.01(a)(i)) could adjust the share.

positions.lease_says: Tenant posts cash or an unconditional irrevocable letter of credit, which Landlord may draw after a default beyond notice and cure, or immediately on bankruptcy or insolvency events.
quotes: Upon the execution and delivery of this Lease, Tenant shall deliver to Landlord either cash or an unconditional irrevocable letter of credit

If Tenant defaults in the full and prompt payment and performance of any of Tenant’s covenants and obligations under this Lease, including, but not limited to, the payment of Fixed Annual Rent and Additional Rent, beyond notice

positions.lease_says: Tenant carries $10 million per occurrence CGL naming Landlord and its designees as additional insureds, and both parties obtain waivers of subrogation.
quotes: A Commercial General Liability insurance policy naming Landlord and its designees as additional insureds
$10,000,000, per occurrence for bodily injury & property damage
pursuant to which the respective insurance companies waive subrogation against each other and any other parties

positions.lease_says: Tenant broadly indemnifies for its acts, occurrences in the Premises and its business, while Landlord indemnifies only for its negligence or willful misconduct in operating the common areas.

positions.why: The letter of credit, the draw right and the burn-down condition all match the standard position. The Security Amount figure is a defined term not set out in the text.

positions.lease_says: Tenant carries $1,000,000 per occurrence of liability insurance, Landlord is not named as an additional insured, and only Landlord waives recovery rights.
positions.proposed_response: Raise the commercial general liability limits to at least $5,000,000 per occurrence, primary plus umbrella. Require that Landlord and its managing agent be named as additional insureds. Make the waiver of subrogation mutual.
quotes: Tenant shall maintain commercial general liability insurance with limits of not less than One Million Dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence.
Landlord waives all rights of recovery against Tenant for any loss covered by Landlord's property insurance.
positions.why: The limit is below $5 million, there is no additional insured requirement, and the waiver of subrogation runs only in Tenant's favor, which meets all three departure triggers.

positions.lease_says: The lease contains no indemnification provision.
positions.why: Neither party gives an indemnity anywhere in the lease. Tenant's indemnity for its use of the premises should be added rather than inferred from silence.

positions.lease_says: Landlord is liable for all damages from its breach, expressly including consequential damages and lost profits, with no limit to its interest in the Building.
positions.proposed_response: Replace Section 11.1 to limit Tenant's recovery to Landlord's interest in the Building, and exclude Landlord's liability for consequential damages and lost profits.
quotes: Landlord shall be liable to Tenant for all damages, including consequential damages and lost profits, arising from Landlord's breach of this Lease.
positions.why: The clause exposes Landlord to consequential damages and does not limit recovery to Landlord's interest in the Building.

positions.lease_says: The lease uses the term Event of Default but does not define it or set any notice and cure periods.
positions.why: No default or cure provision appears in the lease. Monetary and non-monetary cure periods should be added rather than inferred from silence.

positions.lease_says: Landlord restores after a casualty, rent abates only for the unusable part, and Tenant may terminate only if restoration is not substantially complete within 15 months.
quotes: Rent shall abate in proportion to the part of the Premises rendered unusable.
If Landlord has not substantially completed the restoration within fifteen (15) months after the casualty, Tenant may terminate this Lease by notice to Landlord.
positions.why: The 15-month termination trigger exceeds the 12-month minimum, and abatement is limited to the unusable space.

positions.lease_says: Holdover rent equals 100 percent of the last month's Rent, and Tenant is not liable for any other damages.
positions.proposed_response: Raise holdover rent to at least 150 percent of the last month's Rent, increasing after 30 to 60 days. Make Tenant liable for Landlord's damages, including consequential damages, if it holds over past a short grace period after notice.
quotes: Tenant shall pay for each month of holdover the Rent in effect for the last month of the Term, and Tenant shall not be liable for any other damages.
positions.why: Holdover rent is below 150 percent and never escalates. Tenant is also fully released from damages, including consequential damages.

positions.lease_says: Tenant has no renewal, extension, expansion or early termination rights.
quotes: Tenant shall have no option to renew or extend the Term, no right to lease additional space in the Building and no right to terminate this Lease before the Expiration Date.
positions.why: The lease grants none of the options the standard position excludes. First-offer and first-refusal rights are not mentioned, but none are granted either.

positions.lease_says: Delaware law governs, and there is no jury waiver.
positions.proposed_response: Change the governing law to New York and add a mutual waiver of trial by jury.
quotes: This Lease shall be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware.
positions.why: The governing law is Delaware rather than New York, and the lease has no mutual waiver of trial by jury despite the article heading.
